title: Cold rebuild: who is listening, and where?
summary: Read ss -tlnp on a real machine: ports, loopback-only services and PIDs, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Probing the network* you read real listening sockets with `ss`. Now do it again
from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; typing them cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: From your laptop, `curl http://10.0.0.5:5000` says *Connection refused*. On the server, `curl localhost:5000` works and `ss -tlnp` shows `127.0.0.1:5000 dotnet`. What's wrong?
options: The app listens only on loopback; bind it to 0.0.0.0 (e.g. `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:5000`) or put a reverse proxy in front
steps.explain: Refused (not a timeout) means the host answered but nothing listens on that address:port. A timeout would point to a firewall.

steps.title: Who is listening, cold
prompt: Three services run again. Into `~/answers/`, one value per line, smallest first:
2. `loopback-only.txt`: the ports that listen on `127.0.0.1` only.
3. `pid-9100.txt`: the PID of the process on port 9100.
From memory: no hints this time.
